title: Google, the Family calendar and PhirstMaxx: your steps

intro.verdict_html:
Publish the Google app. Publishing lets nobody into Mycelium and lets nobody read your calendar. It only stops Google ending your sign-in every seven days.

One real gap exists, and it is in Mycelium's own connect code, not in Google's setting. Claude Code closes it in this build (family calendar spec, section 4.5): a signed check on the sign-in and a list of allowed Google accounts with one entry, yours.

The rest of this page is the account and key setup the build would otherwise stop and ask you for. Phases 1 and 2 are the ones worth doing tonight.

cells: Only Google accounts you list as test users
Any Google account, for its own calendar only, and only someone already signed in to Mycelium can reach the button
Until you revoke it, or six months unused
Use this, with the code lock in spec 4.5
Only accounts inside your Google Workspace organisation
Needs a paid Workspace. Not offered to a personal Gmail.

prerequisites: Sign-in to the Google account Mycelium is connected with
Kirsty and her phone, for five minutes
A card, only for phase 4 (real public-transport times)
cost: Phase 4 puts a card on file but stays at £0 with the caps in step 4.4

phases.title: Publish the Google app and lock it down
phases.lede_html: You have already reconnected. If that was before publishing, that sign-in still ends in seven days, so step 1.4 does it once more.

steps.title: Find the right project

where.label: Google Cloud → Google Auth Platform → Clients

steps.body_html: Use the project picker in the top bar. The right project is the one whose Clients list has a Web application client with the redirect address below. Stay in that project for the whole phase, and type its name in the box.

blocks.label: The redirect address to look for

steps.title: Trim the redirect addresses

where.label: Google Auth Platform → Clients → your web client

steps.body_html: Open the web client. Under Authorised redirect URIs keep the production address below and any http://localhost:…/api/google/callback entries you use for local work. Delete every other host, old Vercel preview addresses included. Authorised JavaScript origins can be empty. Press Save.

notes.html: Google delivers a sign-in code only to an address on this list. With your own domain as the only public entry, a code for this app cannot be sent anywhere else.

steps.title: Publish the app

where.label: Google Auth Platform → Audience → Publishing status

steps.body_html: Press Publish app, then Confirm. The status changes to In production. Ignore any prompt to submit for verification: Google does not require it for a personal app with fewer than 100 users. If it already says In production, type that and move on.

notes.html: What this changes: Google stops limiting sign-in to a test-user list, so tokens stop expiring weekly. What it does not change: Mycelium's own login still guards the connect button, and a Google sign-in only ever grants access to the calendar of the person who pressed Allow. Nobody gains a route to yours.

steps.title: Reconnect once more, after publishing
steps.body_html: Press RECONNECT and choose your account. On Google hasn't verified this app press Advanced, then Go to … (unsafe), then Continue. That screen means the app has not been through Google's public review, which a private app never needs. Skip this step only if tonight's reconnect came after step 1.3.

steps.title: Name the one Google account Mycelium may accept
steps.body_html: Type the Google address you connected with in 1.4. Claude Code makes it the only account the connect flow accepts, and step 6.1 puts it in the environment.

verify_html: Audience shows Publishing status: In production.
Mycelium → Settings shows Google connected, with no Reconnect needed.
myaccount.google.com/connections lists your app with access to Google Calendar and nothing else.
Eight days from now it is still connected. The daily health check in the build (spec 4.4) messages you if it is not.
phases.why_html: A Google sign-in is a grant from one person to one app for that person's own data. Publishing widens who may give a grant; it never hands anyone somebody else's data. Your calendar is reachable only through the token held in Mycelium's database, and only Mycelium's server, which holds the client secret, can use that token. The seven-day expiry existed because Google treats a Testing app as a throwaway.

phases.title: Kirsty's account and the Family calendar
phases.lede_html: This works on both phones tonight, before any Mycelium build. The build then joins the same calendar to the Family calendar inside Mycelium.

steps.title: Create Kirsty's Google account
steps.body_html: Create the address below with Kirsty choosing the password. Add her mobile as the recovery phone, then turn on 2-Step Verification at myaccount.google.com/signinoptions/twosv.

notes.html: Her password stays with her. Mycelium never signs in as Kirsty; it only shares one calendar to her address.

steps.title: Add the account to her Android phone

where.label: Kirsty's phone → Settings → Passwords & accounts → Add account → Google

steps.body_html: Sign in with the new address and leave Calendar sync on. Open the Google Calendar app (install it from the Play Store if it is missing). Her email can stay in Outlook; this adds a calendar and nothing else.

steps.title: Create the Family calendar in your account

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → Add calendar → Create new calendar

steps.body_html: On a computer, signed in as {{google_account}} (check the avatar, top right). Time zone: (GMT+00:00) United Kingdom Time. Press Create calendar.

steps.title: Share it to Kirsty with edit rights

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → Family → Share with specific people or groups

steps.body_html: In the left column under Settings for my calendars click Family, then Share with specific people or groups → Add people and groups. Paste her address, set the permission to Make changes to events, press Send.

notes.html: Not Make changes and manage sharing: that would let the calendar be shared onward or deleted from her side. Leave Make available to public unticked. Sharing this one calendar shows her nothing of your main calendar or any other.

steps.title: Kirsty accepts

where.label: Kirsty's phone → Gmail → the email from Google Calendar

steps.body_html: She taps Add this calendar in the email. Until she does, the calendar does not appear for her. Then in the Google Calendar app: menu (☰) → tick Family.

steps.title: Show it on your iPhone
steps.body_html: Apple Calendar: open the link, tick Family, press Save. Then Calendar app → Calendars → tick Family under your Google account. Google Calendar app: menu (☰) → tick Family; the link is not needed.

steps.title: Copy the calendar's ID

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → Family → Integrate calendar

steps.body_html: Copy Calendar ID into the box. It ends @group.calendar.google.com. It is an address, not a secret. Mycelium's picker will list your calendars anyway; this removes any doubt about which one.

steps.title: Verify the Mycelium domain for instant updates (optional)

where.label: Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Domain verification

steps.body_html: Google only sends push notifications ("a change happened, come and look") to a web address whose domain is verified in the Cloud project. Press Add domain, enter the Mycelium production domain (the host part of the Vercel URL, no https://), and follow the Search Console flow: the easiest proof is the TXT record it gives you, added at the DNS provider. Without this step the Family calendar still syncs; it polls Google every fifteen minutes instead of hearing within seconds, and Family → Calendar says so.

notes.html: The TXT record is a proof of ownership, not a secret, and it can stay in DNS. Verification is per Cloud project, so it needs doing once.

verify_html: Kirsty adds an event called Test to Family on her phone. It shows on your iPhone within a minute.
You move it by an hour on your phone. Hers follows.
On her phone, none of your other calendars is listed.

Family → Calendar in Mycelium says "Instant updates from Google are on" (after the build, once the calendar is chosen). If it says the 15-minute poll is doing the work, the domain is not verified yet.
phases.why_html: Google shares calendars one at a time. Family is a separate container in your account, so edit rights on it say nothing about your primary calendar. Both phones talk straight to Google, which is why this works before Mycelium is involved. Mycelium then becomes a third reader and writer of the same calendar.

phases.title: Free keys: routing and YouTube
phases.lede_html: Neither needs a card. Keep each key in its tab or your password manager until phase 6.

steps.title: OpenRouteService key
steps.body_html: Create the account (it is a HeiGIT account), confirm the email, sign in. The dashboard shows a free Standard key; if it shows none, request a free token and name it Mycelium. The free plan allows 2,000 route requests a day and 40 a minute. Commercial use is not allowed on it, which is fine for a personal app.

notes.html: The key goes into phase 6 and nowhere else. Not this page, not a chat.

steps.title: Turn on the YouTube Data API

where.label: Google Cloud → APIs & Services → Library → YouTube Data API v3

steps.body_html: Same project as phase 1 ({{gcp_project}}). Press Enable. No billing account is needed.

steps.title: Create a key that can only call YouTube
steps.body_html: Create credentials → API key. Under API restrictions choose Restrict key and tick only YouTube Data API v3. Leave Application restrictions on None: the calls come from Vercel, which has no fixed address. Save and copy the key.

notes.html: An API key reads public YouTube information only. It carries no access to your Google account, and the restriction makes a leaked key useless for anything else.

verify_html: The OpenRouteService dashboard lists one key with the Standard plan.
Credentials lists Mycelium YouTube with one API under Restrictions.
Both keys are tested for real in step 6.3.
phases.why_html: PhirstMaxx needs door-to-door times from each of your start points, and it needs a video's title, description and location tags to work out which place it is about. OpenRouteService answers the first for driving, walking and cycling from open map data. YouTube's own API answers the second without scraping a page.

phases.title: Google Maps key (optional, needs a card)
phases.lede_html: Only for real public-transport times and Google's place details. Without it PhirstMaxx still gives drive, walk and cycle times and estimates public transport from research. To leave it for now, answer 4.1 with later and tick the rest of the phase.

steps.title: Decide: now or later
steps.body_html: Google gives each Maps product its own free allowance every month: 10,000 calls on the basic tier, 5,000 on Pro, 1,000 on Enterprise. Two people will not approach that. The catch is that Google issues the key only to a project with a billing account, and a billing account needs a card.

steps.title: Add a billing account
steps.body_html: Create a billing account (country United Kingdom, your card) and link it to {{gcp_project}}. Google may place a small temporary hold to check the card.

steps.title: Enable the two APIs

where.label: Google Cloud → APIs & Services → Library → Routes API

steps.body_html: Press Enable on Routes API, then the same on Places API (New). Enable nothing else.

steps.title: Cap it so the bill cannot leave £0
steps.body_html: For Routes API and Places API (New), set every per-day request quota to 30. That is at most 930 calls a month on each, under the smallest free allowance (1,000). Then at Billing → Budgets & alerts create a budget of £1 with email alerts at 50% and 100%. If an API offers only per-minute limits, leave it and say so to Claude Code: Mycelium also counts its own calls and stops at 900 a month per product.

notes.html: A budget only emails you. It does not stop spending. The quota is the hard stop: calls past it fail instead of billing.

steps.title: Create a key that can only call those two
steps.body_html: Create credentials → API key. API restrictions → Restrict key → tick Routes API and Places API (New) only. Save and copy the key.

verify_html: Enabled APIs lists Routes API and Places API (New).
Quotas shows 30 a day on each.
Budgets & alerts shows the £1 budget.
phases.why_html: Google bills per call above a free monthly allowance on each product. A hard daily cap that adds up to less than the smallest allowance means the charge cannot be more than nothing, whatever the app does. Mycelium's own counter is a second stop in case a console limit is ever changed.

phases.title: The old PhirstMaxxing database address
phases.lede_html: The importer reads the live old app so PhirstMaxx starts with your real blocks, plans and ideas. It runs on the PC only. The old repo has no local env file, so the address has to come from Supabase.

steps.title: Copy the connection string
steps.body_html: Pick the PhirstMaxxing project, not Mycelium. Press Connect in the top bar, choose Session pooler, and copy the URI. It holds [YOUR-PASSWORD] as a placeholder.

steps.title: Put the database password in

where.label: Supabase → Database → Settings → Reset database password

steps.body_html: If you do not have that project's database password, press Reset database password, generate one made of letters and digits only, and save it in your password manager. The old app keeps working: it talks to Supabase with API keys, not this password. Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] in the URI with it.

notes.html: This string is full access to the old database. It goes into .env.local on the PC in step 6.1 and nowhere else: not Vercel, not this page, not a chat.

verify_html: The finished URI starts postgresql://postgres. and contains pooler.supabase.com:5432.
It no longer contains square brackets.
Step 6.3 reads a row count through it.
phases.why_html: The session pooler is the address that works from a home connection without IPv6. A reset only affects things that hold the old connection string, and the old app holds none. Keeping the address on the PC means the most powerful secret in this guide never leaves your machine.

phases.title: Put the values where Mycelium reads them

steps.title: The PC: .env.local
steps.body_html: Open the file, add the lines below at the end, and paste each value straight after its = with no quotes and no spaces. Leave out GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY if you answered later in 4.1. Save.

steps.title: Production: Vercel
steps.body_html: Add each name below with its value, Environment Production, and tick Sensitive on the three keys. Do not add the old database address here. No redeploy is needed: Claude Code's next push picks them up.

steps.title: Test all three from the PC
steps.body_html: Each command reads its value from .env.local, so nothing secret is typed or shown. The first routes Doncaster to York by car.

blocks.label: Routing: expect a distance near 60,000 metres and a duration near 3,300 seconds
YouTube: expect Me at the zoo

shells.bash:
cd /a/Projects/Mycelium
k=$(grep -E '^YOUTUBE_API_KEY=' .env.local | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/videos?part=snippet&id=jNQXAC9IVRw&key=$k" | grep -o '"title": "[^"]*"' | head -1

shells.ps:
cd A:\Projects\Mycelium
$u=(Select-String -Path .env.local -Pattern '^PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL=(.+)$').Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
psql $u -c "select count(*) from availability_blocks"
shells.bash:
cd /a/Projects/Mycelium
psql "$(grep -E '^PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL=' .env.local | cut -d= -f2-)" -c "select count(*) from availability_blocks"

verify_html: The routing command prints a distance and a duration.
The YouTube command prints a video title.
The database command prints a count of your availability blocks.
Vercel lists the names under Production.
phases.why_html: .env.local is what the PC worker, the importer and local builds read. Vercel's variables are what production reads. Splitting them this way gives each place only the secrets it uses.

phases.title: Hand back to Claude Code

steps.title: Set the research spend
steps.body_html: Each drop's web research is one paid cloud AI call, a few pence. Either leave it inside the existing £5 monthly AI cap, or give PhirstMaxx a monthly figure of its own. Type your choice.

fields.label: Research spend
fields.placeholder: inside the £5 cap / £3 a month of its own

steps.title: Paste this to Claude Code
steps.body_html: The block fills itself in from the boxes above. Anything still in angle brackets is a box you have not filled; either fill it or tell Claude Code it is missing.

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text:
The files you asked for are in the repo now. claude/family-calendar-spec.md is the Google rewrite (it has 4.4, and a new 4.5 that locks the Google sign-in to my account), and claude/backlog.md has the three sections. Re-read both and claude/phirstmaxx-spec.md, commit them, then build in the order I gave you.

My steps are already done. The checklist is docs/checklists/google-family-phirstmaxx-setup.json: ship it in-app, start its run and set these as its answers, with every step ticked except any marked missing below.
- Google Cloud project: {{gcp_project}}. Publishing status: {{publish_status}}. I reconnected after publishing.
- The only Google account allowed: {{google_account}}. GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS is in .env.local and on Vercel.
- Family calendar ID: {{family_calendar_id}}. Shared to kirstykjpetco@gmail.com with Make changes to events, and she has accepted.
- ORS_API_KEY and YOUTUBE_API_KEY are in .env.local and on Vercel.
- Google Maps key: {{maps_choice}}.
- PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL is in .env.local only.
- Research spend: {{research_cap}}.
- Domain verified for Google push: {{push_domain}}.

Do not stop for any of those. Check each env name is present before relying on it, and stop only for what is missing.

verify_html: Claude Code reports that it has committed the three docs and started on the family calendar.
It does not ask again for anything listed in the prompt.
phases.why_html: Claude Code cannot see this page, so the answers travel in the prompt and it writes them into the in-app copy of this checklist, where they stay.

troubleshooting.symptom: Google shows Error 403: access_denied when you reconnect
troubleshooting.cause: The app is still in Testing and the account is not a listed test user
The address Mycelium sends is no longer in the client's list
troubleshooting.fix: Step 1.2: add the production address back exactly as written.

troubleshooting.symptom: Reconnect needed comes back after a week
troubleshooting.cause: The last reconnect was made while the app was still in Testing
troubleshooting.fix: Check 1.3 says In production, then do 1.4 again.

troubleshooting.cause: She has not tapped Add this calendar, or it is unticked in the app's menu
troubleshooting.fix: Step 2.5. If the email is missing, remove her in 2.4 and add her again to send a new one.

troubleshooting.symptom: Family is missing from Apple Calendar on your iPhone
troubleshooting.cause: Google does not pass a new calendar to Apple's app until it is ticked
troubleshooting.fix: Step 2.6, then pull down to refresh in Calendars.

troubleshooting.symptom: The YouTube test says the key is not valid or the API is not enabled
troubleshooting.cause: The API was enabled in a different project from the key, or the key is restricted to another API
troubleshooting.fix: Steps 3.2 and 3.3 in the same project.

troubleshooting.cause: The account email is unconfirmed, or the key was pasted with a space or a line break
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the email, re-copy the key, fix the line in .env.local.

troubleshooting.symptom: A Maps call returns PERMISSION_DENIED or REQUEST_DENIED
troubleshooting.cause: Billing is not linked to the project, or one of the two APIs is not enabled
The placeholder is still in the address, or the password contains @ : / or #
PostgreSQL's folder is not on the PATH
troubleshooting.fix: Use the full path: "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin\psql.exe" in place of psql.
